title: Misconduct investigation against Nolan Wells' mother closed by Mississippi Board of Nursing, she says
text:
Earlier Wednesday, Wonsley’s attorney, civil rights and personal injury lawyer Ben Crump, released a statement condemning the complaint and investigation as a “warning shot” meant to pressure and silence a grieving mother.
JACKSON, Miss. — A professional misconduct investigation against Christine Wells Wonsley, the mother of Nolan Wells, that was initiated following an anonymous complaint, has been closed by the Mississippi Board of Nursing, Wonsley said Wednesday on Facebook.
“This definitely has added more hurt to an already devastating time because I love my job and I love my patients,” Wonsley said in the post. “NOLAN’S CASE IS STILL ONGOING. ” Earlier Wednesday, Wonsley’s attorney, civil rights and personal injury lawyer Ben Crump, released a statementTIMELINE: Here’s what we know about the disappearance and death of 18-year-old Nolan WellsCrump said Wonsley has spent her career caring for Mississippi patients without a prior complaint to the board.
After Nolan’s body was found, Wonsley took leave from her job to bury her son. Crump said it was only after she began asking questions about Nolan’s death that the complaint was filed.
“This is a warning shot at a grieving mother, meant to pressure and scare her into staying quiet,” Crump said in a statement. “It is a distraction, it is intimidation, and we will not let it stand. Christine had part of her identity stolen from her the day Nolan died. Now, someone is trying to take another piece of it.
